officialTitle: Breast International Group 1-98: letrozole versus tamoxifen, alone or in sequence, as adjuvant therapy for postmenopausal women with hormone-receptor-positive early breast cancer

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: A total of 8010 women with data that could be assessed were enrolled, 4003 in the letrozole group and 4007 in the tamoxifen group.
design.notes: Four-arm design: letrozole, tamoxifen, letrozole→tamoxifen, tamoxifen→letrozole (5 years total). Primary core analysis compared initial letrozole with initial tamoxifen; the 2009 report compared sequences with letrozole monotherapy (6182 women) and updated the monotherapy comparison (4922 women).

clinicalQuestion: In postmenopausal women with HR+ early breast cancer, is adjuvant letrozole superior to tamoxifen, and does sequencing the two improve on letrozole alone?

pico.population: Postmenopausal women with hormone-receptor-positive early breast cancer
pico.intervention: Letrozole (monotherapy or in sequence with tamoxifen) for 5 years
pico.comparator: Tamoxifen for 5 years; letrozole monotherapy (for sequence comparisons)
pico.outcomes: Primary: DFS. Secondary: OS, distant recurrence, adverse events

arms.label: Sequential arms
arms.regimen: Letrozole followed by tamoxifen, or tamoxifen followed by letrozole (2 years + 3 years)

publications.title: A comparison of letrozole and tamoxifen in postmenopausal women with early breast cancer.
publications.label: Primary core analysis

publications.title: Letrozole therapy alone or in sequence with tamoxifen in women with breast cancer.
publications.label: Sequential-treatment analysis and updated monotherapy comparison

outcomes.sourceQuote: After a median follow-up of 25.8 months, 351 events had occurred in the letrozole group and 428 events in the tamoxifen group, with five-year disease-free survival estimates of 84.0 percent and 81.4 percent, respectively. As compared with tamoxifen, letrozole significantly reduced the risk of an event ending a period of disease-free survival (hazard ratio, 0.81; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.70 to 0.93; P=0.003), especially the risk of distant recurrence (hazard ratio, 0.73; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.60 to 0.88; P=0.001).

After a median follow-up of 25.8 months, 351 events had occurred in the letrozole group and 428 events in the tamoxifen group, with five-year disease-free survival estimates of 84.0 percent and 81.4 percent, respectively. As compared with tamoxifen, letrozole significantly reduced the risk of an event ending a period of disease-free survival (hazard ratio, 0.81; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.70 to 0.93; P=0.003), especially the risk of distant recurrence (hazard ratio, 0.73; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.60 to 0.88; P=0.001).

At a median follow-up of 71 months after randomization, disease-free survival was not significantly improved with either sequential treatment as compared with letrozole alone (hazard ratio for tamoxifen followed by letrozole, 1.05; 99% confidence interval [CI], 0.84 to 1.32; hazard ratio for letrozole followed by tamoxifen, 0.96; 99% CI, 0.76 to 1.21).

At a median follow-up of 71 months after randomization, disease-free survival was not significantly improved with either sequential treatment as compared with letrozole alone (hazard ratio for tamoxifen followed by letrozole, 1.05; 99% confidence interval [CI], 0.84 to 1.32; hazard ratio for letrozole followed by tamoxifen, 0.96; 99% CI, 0.76 to 1.21).

The updated analysis of monotherapy showed that there was a nonsignificant difference in overall survival between women assigned to treatment with letrozole and those assigned to treatment with tamoxifen (hazard ratio for letrozole, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.75 to 1.02; P=0.08).

safety.sourceQuote: Thromboembolism, endometrial cancer, and vaginal bleeding were more common in the tamoxifen group. Women given letrozole had a higher incidence of skeletal and cardiac events and of hypercholesterolemia.

strengths: Directly addresses both agent choice and sequencing
limitations: Early primary analysis with short median follow-up
Selective crossover from tamoxifen to letrozole after initial results complicates long-term monotherapy comparisons
Overall survival difference not statistically significant in the 2009 update

clinicalImplications.text: Established letrozole as a preferred adjuvant endocrine option over tamoxifen in postmenopausal HR+ early breast cancer, and showed no disease-free survival advantage for routine switching strategies over letrozole monotherapy.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Sequencing tamoxifen then letrozole was not superior to letrozole alone, and early relapses were more frequent when tamoxifen came first — favour upfront AI in higher-risk postmenopausal patients.

curation.notes: Numbers transcribed from PubMed abstracts of PMIDs 16382061 and 19692688. PubMed lists a corporate first author for both, so firstAuthor is omitted. Arm sizes are those of the primary core analysis.
